summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after allogeneic cord transplant, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure, was readmitted for diarrhea, vomiting, and weakness following recent exposure to ill family members. He was diagnosed with likely acute gastrointestinal infection, though stool studies were negative for common pathogens and adenovirus PCR remained pending at discharge. His symptoms resolved with supportive care, including IV fluids and a low-residue diet. Acute on chronic kidney injury, likely prerenal from volume loss, improved with hydration, and hyperkalemia resolved. His heart failure was managed with temporary discontinuation and subsequent reduction of Lasix to 40 mg daily. He remained stable for GVHD without steroid escalation and was discharged home with services, with plans to follow up on pending viral studies and medication management.
